The main takeaway from our work is that

the neural representation of expected values (EV) in the human brain is not unitary but rather involves a distributed set of brain regions, with the nucleus accumbens representing the affective (i.e., magnitude) component and the medial prefrontal cortex representing the probabilistic (i.e., probability) component of expected value.
the neural representation of expected utility (or expected value, or subjective value) is not limited to the ventral striatum.
